advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Thread repo_root into _effective_status_map_for → config.effective_status_map(project_key, root=repo_root) so outbound mapping reads the same config as the fetcher known-set and preflight.
evidence: outbound_differ.py:281: `    return config.effective_status_map(project_key)` — no root argument
config.py:77: `def effective_status_map(project_key: str, root: object = None)` then `cfg = mc.load_mapping_config(root)` with root=None → CWD-based discovery via `_discover_project_config(root)`
fetcher.py: `_known_jira_statuses(repo_root)` and reconcile.py:485 `preflight_status_mapping(mutations, repo_root)` both thread repo_root explicitly
run_differs.py:195: `cwd=str(repo_root)` shows CWD is NOT assumed equal to repo_root
advisory.finding: outbound_differ._effective_status_map_for resolves the effective status map with config.effective_status_map(project_key) and NO repo_root, so the [mapping] config is discovered from the current working directory, whereas the sibling fetcher known-set (_known_jira_statuses(repo_root)) and preflight (preflight_status_mapping(..., repo_root)) resolve the SAME config against the pass's repo_root. When CWD != repo_root the outbound status mapping and the known-set/preflight can read different configs.
scenarios: A reconcile pass invoked with a repo_root differing from the process CWD
A per-project status_map that is only present in the repo_root config file
advisory.suggested_fix: Pass repo_root through compute_outbound_mutations/OutboundDiffConfig into _effective_status_map_for and call config.effective_status_map(project_key, root=repo_root).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Throttle/dedup the resolve_outbound_status drift warning (or route it through the existing dedup alert path) so a persistent drift does not re-warn every pass.
evidence: outbound_mapper.py: `if target is None:` then `print(f"rebar-reconciler: local status {value!r} has no Jira target ...", file=sys.stderr)` with no dedup/throttle
fetcher.py `_flag_unmapped_statuses` docstring: '(24h window) so a persistent unmapped status does not re-file every ~20-minute pass'
advisory.finding: resolve_outbound_status emits an unconditional, unthrottled stderr warning every time a local status has no Jira target, so a persistently drifting/SKIPped status re-prints the drift alert on every reconcile pass (~every 20 min) — unlike _flag_unmapped_statuses which dedups over a 24h window.
scenarios: A project intentionally SKIPs a status; every pass then re-emits the same stderr line for every affected ticket

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the stamp-rule docstring to say the built-in set is {blocked, cancelled, deleted} (deleted is lossy), or explicitly justify why deleted is excluded upstream.
evidence: outbound_labels.py: docstring 'On the built-in map this selects exactly {blocked, cancelled}'
config.py:49: `"deleted": "Done"` and config.py:72: `"Done": "closed"` → deleted reverse-maps to closed, so _desired_status_annotation('deleted', None) returns 'rebar-status:deleted'
_field_contract.py:75: `lossy_values=frozenset({"blocked", "cancelled", "deleted"})` confirms deleted is lossy
advisory.finding: The generalised stamp rule (_desired_status_annotation) selects {blocked, cancelled, deleted} on the built-in map, not 'exactly {blocked, cancelled}' as the docstring and commit message claim: deleted maps to 'Done' and jira_to_local_status['Done'] == 'closed' != 'deleted', so it is lossy and would be stamped rebar-status:deleted.
scenarios: A ticket with status 'deleted' reaching the annotation-label diff (normally excluded via excluded_statuses={'archived','deleted'}, so impact is low)

blocking.finding: The new outbound_differ integration seam `_effective_status_map_for` (project-key resolution + threading the effective status map into both the CREATE and UPDATE paths, wired via `mapping=config.projects_mapping`) has no test. Every test in the new suite injects `status_map=eff` directly into the mapper/label helpers, bypassing the resolution and threading wiring, and none drives `compute_outbound_mutations`.
